newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end week in record territory.
newsitem.headline: German shares end week in record territory.

text.p: German shares ended the week on a bullish note, as the firm dollar and an unexpected drop in U.S. unemployment propelled the blue chip DAX into record territory on Friday.

After-hours trade saw the IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic dealing in blue chip shares, build on a solid day's gains to close up 0.43 percent at 3,700.53 points -- the first ever close above the crucial 3,700 point level.
Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade up 22.26 points at 3,695.29 points, after hitting a new lifetime high at 3,708.25.
The U.S. jobless rate unexpectedly fell to 4.8 percent in May, its lowest level since October 1973, giving fresh impetus to the dollar in late trade -- always good news for German exporters.

Among the day's most notable movers was carbon and graphite group SGL Carbon which ended bourse trade down 21.20 marks at 239 marks on news that authorities in Europe and the US were investigating the group for alleged price fixing.

SGL Carbon, which had become a clear market favourite since its bourse listing two years ago, said it would participate in the investigation but denied wrongdoing. The shares ended IBIS trade at 236.90 marks.
Among other shares, chemical stocks including Hoechst AG, Bayer AG and BASF AG all traded higher, enjoying the prospect of a firmer dollar which makes their exports cheaper abroad.

Deutsche Telekom shares ended bourse trade up 1.00 marks at 40.15 marks, and rose to 40.20 marks in IBIS trade, gaining on follow-through support from a buy recommendation from U.S. securities house Salomon Brothers.
